1000800.etyen:
As a place name, from the common noun bø (“farm; enclosed farmland, infield”), inherited from Old Norse bǿr (“farm, farmstead”). The Old Norse noun is from the root of búa (“to dwell, reside”), from Proto-Germanic *būaną (“to dwell, reside”), ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *bʰuH- (“to be, grow”). The name is widespread in Norway, especially as a farm name.
The surname is habitational, from one of the many Norwegian farms named Bø.

The first element continues Old Norse guð (“God, god”), also goð, from Proto-Germanic *gudą (“god”); its further origin is disputed. The verb derives from Middle Low German schēn (“to happen”), ultimately from Proto-Germanic *skehaną (“to move quickly; happen”), from Proto-Indo-European *skek- (“to move quickly, jump”). en.g: a mountain in Lom municipality, Innlandet, Norway, in Jotunheimen; the highest mountain in Norway and Northern Europe

1004384.etyen:
From Galdhøe (“mountain in Jotunheimen”) + pigg (“peak, spike”), with the second element in the definite singular piggen (“the peak”). The name Galdhøe is from the farm name Galde in Bøverdalen, with gald (“steep mountain road, mountain path”) + hø (“rounded, dome-shaped mountain”).
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk Galdhøpiggen (“mountain in Lom, Norway”).

1004640.etyen: From the officially standardized Norwegian place-name element Trifan-, representing a local adaptation of Russian Трифон (Trifon), from Ancient Greek Τρύφων (Trúphōn, “delicate; one who lives softly or luxuriously”), ultimately from Ancient Greek τρυφάω (trupháō, “to live softly or luxuriously”), itself from Ancient Greek τρυφή (truphḗ, “softness, delicacy; luxury”), and the definite singular of bekk (“stream, brook”). The name refers to Saint Tryphon of Pechenga.
